candidates.name: Index map: official search (PG10)
verified_facts: Last updated 20 July 2026.
Section 7.1 was amended because of a practice change intended to reduce rejections caused by mismatches between the shapefile and the search-of-index-map plan.
The guide explains information held on the index map and official search procedure.
semantic_limits: Index-map/search-plan evidence is a registration/search control and is not an exact legal-boundary or terrain-height measurement.

candidates.name: HM Land Registry plans: boundaries (PG40s3)
verified_facts: Updated 1 June 2026.
The guide separately covers difficulties in showing the precise position of physical boundaries, identifying the legal boundary and the general-boundaries rule.
Boundary structures and legal boundary position are distinct concepts in the guide.
semantic_limits: INSPIRE polygons or ordinary title-plan edging must not be promoted to an exact legal-boundary claim without determined-boundary evidence.

candidates.name: Boundary agreements and determined boundaries (PG40s4)
verified_facts: Updated 1 June 2026.
Measurements on determined-boundary plans must be accurate to +/-10 mm and taken horizontally from defined permanent features.
Where National Grid coordinates are used, the guide requires absolute accuracy of +/-300 mm and relative accuracy of +/-10 mm.
semantic_limits: These determined-boundary survey tolerances are not automatically applicable to ordinary INSPIRE polygons or title-plan edging.

candidates.name: Title plan (PG40s5)
verified_facts: Updated 13 July 2026.
The title plan must be read with the register and documents referred to by the register.
Usual title-plan scales are 1:1250 urban and 1:2500 rural.
Dimensions shown on a title plan provide only an additional indication and the title plan still shows the general boundary.
semantic_limits: Title-plan dimensions and red edging are not treated as exact parcel-boundary coordinates unless the boundary has been determined through the appropriate process.

candidates.name: Plan requirements and surveying specification (PG41s5)
verified_facts: The guide requires plans to be based on an accurate survey plotted at the stated scale.
It gives plottable-limit tolerances of 0.3 mm at map scale plus one part in one thousand of measured distance.
Survey control stations should preserve the datum used for the original survey.
semantic_limits: Developer-plan survey tolerances are a plan-QA reference and do not prove that the current INSPIRE polygon or LiDAR raster was surveyed to those tolerances.

candidates.name: Basis of HM Land Registry plans (PG40s1)
verified_facts: Ordnance Survey mapping shows topographic features and is not intended to represent property boundaries.
The guide states that a line on a 1:1250 map roughly represents 0.3 m on the ground and a line on a 1:2500 map roughly represents 0.6 m.
HM Land Registry does not provide scaled measurements from title plans or OS mapping.
semantic_limits: Map-scale positional tolerance is horizontal plan evidence and must not be merged into LiDAR vertical RMSE.

candidates.name: Preparing plans for applications (PG40s2)
verified_facts: The parent guide was last updated 13 October 2025.
Plans should be accurately drawn to a stated scale, show orientation and contain sufficient surrounding detail to identify the land on OS mapping.
Reduced or distorted plans that retain the original scale endorsement can be rejected.
semantic_limits: Plan acceptability does not convert deed-plan graphics into exact terrain-height observations.

candidates.name: Other plan-related services and guides (PG40s6)
verified_facts: The official search of the index map service is separate from the official copy service for title plans and registers.
Illustrative plans are used to visualise relative locations of titles revealed by SIM results.
The guide points users to PG10 for index-map searches and PG11 for title-plan copies.
semantic_limits: Illustrative/SIM outputs are not substituted for the exact HMLR polygon or terrain raster used by this slot.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 grid data
verified_facts: Each grid height is calculated as a mean of heights across the whole 5 m pixel.
ASCII z values are positioned 2.5 m from the tile corner to represent the pixel centre.
Height values are stored to the nearest 0.01 m.
Per-tile metadata includes flying-date information.
semantic_limits: 0.01 m storage precision and 5 m grid geometry are not equivalent to 0.01 m measurement accuracy.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 contour data
verified_facts: Contour data is supplied as GML 3.2.1 and per-tile metadata.
Spot heights are selected by an automated process from closed contours.
Spot-height z values are rounded to one decimal place and genuine depressions can produce a spot height below surrounding contours.
semantic_limits: Contour and spot-height products remain secondary diagnostic evidence and are not used as the primary parcel height-difference source.

candidates.name: The National Grid reference convention
verified_facts: The National Grid uses a false origin southwest of the Scilly Isles so British coordinates are positive.
The grid is divided into 100 km squares identified by two-letter codes.
Grid references combine the square code with easting and northing values.
semantic_limits: Grid-reference parsing validates tile identity only; it does not add vertical accuracy.

candidates.name: Ordnance Datum Newlyn
verified_facts: ODN is the national mainland height datum.
OS warns that traditional bench marks can be affected by subsidence, with metre-scale cases reported in some mining areas.
The page gives separate statistical levelling-error expectations for benchmark classes.
semantic_limits: Benchmark-network accuracy and subsidence are not used to shrink the EA LiDAR raster RMSE.

candidates.name: National Geoid Model OSGM15
verified_facts: OSGM15 converts ETRS89 ellipsoid height to orthometric datum heights including ODN on mainland Britain.
The geoid model uses a 1 km grid with bilinear interpolation.
Nominal mainland geoid-model accuracy is 8 mm RMS.
semantic_limits: OSGM15 geoid-model accuracy is separate from terrain-surface measurement error and cannot be used to reduce the LiDAR RMSE.

candidates.name: Coordinate reference systems - cartography guide
verified_facts: A coordinate transformation is required to move positions between CRSs.
The OS example states that ETRS89 GNSS positions should pass through OSTN15 to become OSGB36 National Grid coordinates.
Transformation complexity can range from simple shifts to grid-based rubber-sheet operations.
semantic_limits: CRS transformation correctness is horizontal-position QA and remains separate from elevation-source uncertainty.

candidates.name: LIDAR Composite Catalogues
verified_facts: The dataset is described as indices for full-coverage LIDAR surveys of England.
It is published by the Environment Agency.
The catalogue page itself exposes no terrain data service or downloadable height resource.
semantic_limits: Catalogue membership is lineage/coverage evidence only and cannot be sampled as elevation.

candidates.name: LIDAR Composite First Return DSM 2m
verified_facts: The first-return DSM is a 2 m raster covering about 99% of England.
It includes vehicles, buildings and vegetation as well as terrain where the first return is ground.
The national-programme surveys are feathered across overlaps and the product does not necessarily match the coverage of the last-return DSM composite.
Individual input surveys have +/-15 cm RMSE vertical accuracy.
semantic_limits: First-return DSM 2 m is excluded from the primary bare-earth result and used only as a surface-object diagnostic.

candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue projection information
verified_facts: EA data is supplied in OSGB36 British National Grid with elevations above Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
For time-stamped and point-cloud data, EA directs users to metadata catalogues for the specific geoid model used by a survey.
Surveys carried out after 26 August 2016 use OSGM15.
semantic_limits: A survey-period geoid model must be read from lineage metadata; a modern datum assumption is not silently back-applied to older surveys.

candidates.name: Retired LIDAR Composite DTM 2017 - 25cm
verified_facts: The 25 cm composite is explicitly marked retired and no longer available on the Data Services Platform.
EA states that it no longer produces a 25 cm composite and that it has been replaced by a 1 m version.
Historic 25 cm time-stamped data remains part of the archive even though the 25 cm composite is retired.
semantic_limits: Retired composite data is rejected as the current canonical primary source; historical time-stamped use requires explicit survey lineage.
